description: The US slice of Mynt's regulatory model for money transmission, digital-asset on-ramps and off-ramps and buy-and-hold stablecoin products. Researched 2026-11-07 from primary-domain sources (see each instrument's url); the full text of the pages could not be opened from the research session, so check each against its source before relying on it. Coverage is checked per state for a product that lists the states it's offered in (offered_in, ISO 3166-2 codes like 'us-ny'): a state regulator carries its jurisdiction, and its licences cover only that state; a federal licence covers every state only when its covers says 'us', and each such claim says in its coverage_note what is assumed and still to verify. Money transmission is licensed by each state: the FinCEN money services business registration covers no state by itself (covers: []) and is a prerequisite (requires) of each state's money transmitter licence, which counts only alongside it. To add a state's money transmitter licence: add (or reuse) its regulator with jurisdiction 'us-xx' and short_name in region_definition; add a licence type '<regulator>_money_transmitter' granting us_money_transmission (sale, servicing) with requires set to the FinCEN registration, its application procedure (most states license through NMLS), and one obligation citing the state's money transmission act, added to legislation with its url; record in coverage_note what is assumed (exemptions such as agent of the payee, and whether virtual-currency transmission needs a separate licence there). Take every fact from the state's own sources; never invent licence numbers, bond or net-worth amounts. OFAC, CFPB and IRS obligations are kept on the FinCEN registration's register, the registration every ramp and exchange holds. State money transmitter licences are modelled for every state and the District of Columbia; the state entries were researched from public sources on 2026-11-08 and each licence's coverage_note names its main source and what is still to verify. Montana is kept as a regulator (mt_dbfi) with no licence types, because Montana has no money transmitter licence: Montana has no money transmitter licence. The Division (part of the Montana Department of Administration) states that it does not regulate money transmitters and that money transmission is not defined under Montana law (Division page and its article of 2023-04-12, 'The Challenge of Being the Only State Not Regulating Money Transmitters'). This does not mean no Montana licence is needed: depending on the activity, a consumer finance, escrow, retail sales finance or other Montana licence may apply, and the Division points applicants to NMLS and their own counsel. The FinCEN money services business registration still applies federally. To verify: that no Montana bill enacted after 2023 created a money transmitter licence (none was found on official sources as of 2026-11-08; check bills.legmt.gov). Source: https://doa.mt.gov/BFID/.

product_categories.name: Money transmission
product_categories.description: Moving money or value for others, including convertible virtual currency: on-ramps and off-ramps.

product_categories.name: Virtual currency
product_categories.description: Buying and selling convertible virtual currency, including stablecoins, for customers.

regulated_product_types.name: Money transmission, including convertible virtual currency (on-ramp and off-ramp)
regulated_product_types.description: Accepting US dollars or convertible virtual currency from a customer and transmitting it, including turning dollars into a stablecoin and back for the customer.

regulated_product_types.name: Money transmission (US dollars)
regulated_product_types.description: Receiving US dollars from a customer and transmitting them to another person or place, or holding them in transit for the customer (e.g. by bank transfer in and out), as each state's money transmission law defines it.

legislation.title: Bank Secrecy Act definitions: money transmitter
legislation.summary: A money transmitter accepts currency, funds or value that substitutes for currency from one person and transmits it to another location or person by any means, unless an exemption in (ff)(5)(ii) applies.

legislation.title: Registration of money services businesses
legislation.summary: Register with FinCEN (Form 107) within 180 days of being established, renew every two years, re-register on certain changes, and keep an agent list.

legislation.title: Anti-money laundering programs for money services businesses
legislation.summary: A written, risk-based AML program with internal controls, a compliance officer, training and independent review.

legislation.title: Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions
legislation.summary: Report suspicious transactions of $2,000 or more within 30 calendar days of initial detection; keep records five years.

legislation.title: Currency transaction reports
legislation.summary: Report each transaction in currency of more than $10,000, aggregating one person's transactions in a business day, within 15 days.

legislation.title: Funds transfer recordkeeping and the Travel Rule
legislation.summary: For transmittals of funds of $3,000 or more, keep the required records and pass the required information to the next institution.

legislation.title: Retention of Bank Secrecy Act records
legislation.summary: Keep required records for five years, accessible within a reasonable time.

legislation.title: Application of FinCEN's regulations to certain business models involving convertible virtual currencies
legislation.summary: An exchanger or administrator that accepts and transmits convertible virtual currency, or buys or sells it for any reason, is a money transmitter unless an exemption applies.

legislation.title: Sanctions compliance guidance for the virtual currency industry
legislation.summary: Sanctions obligations apply equally to virtual currency and fiat transactions; OFAC recommends a risk-based sanctions compliance program.

legislation.title: Reporting, procedures and penalties regulations
legislation.summary: Report blocked property within 10 business days and annually as of June 30 by September 30; report rejected transactions within 10 business days.

legislation.title: Regulation E: procedures for resolving errors
legislation.summary: Investigate a consumer's notice of an electronic fund transfer error within 10 business days (up to 45 days with provisional credit) and correct it within one business day.

legislation.title: Gross proceeds and basis reporting by brokers of digital assets
legislation.summary: Brokers report gross proceeds on Form 1099-DA for sales from 2025 and basis for covered assets from 2026, with an optional aggregate method for qualifying stablecoins.

legislation.title: Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act)
legislation.summary: Only a permitted payment stablecoin issuer may issue a payment stablecoin in the US; 1:1 reserves, monthly reserve reports and published redemption policies. From 2028-07-18 a digital asset service provider may not offer or sell to US persons a payment stablecoin not issued by a permitted issuer. Effective the earlier of 2027-01-18 or 120 days after final rules.

legislation.title: OCC rule implementing the GENIUS Act (12 CFR part 15)
legislation.summary: Licensing, reserves, redemption and supervision for OCC-supervised permitted payment stablecoin issuers.

legislation.title: GENIUS Act regulations on payment stablecoin issuance, offer and sale (proposed)
legislation.summary: Proposed rule under section 3; comments closed 2026-10-19.

legislation.title: Virtual currencies (BitLicense)
legislation.summary: No one may engage in virtual currency business activity involving New York or a New York resident without a licence: capital, custody, books and records, financial reports, AML, cybersecurity, consumer disclosures and complaints.

legislation.title: Cybersecurity requirements for financial services companies
legislation.summary: Annual certification of compliance by April 15, and notice of a cybersecurity incident within 72 hours.

legislation.title: Guidance on the issuance of U.S. dollar-backed stablecoins
legislation.summary: Reserves at least equal to outstanding coins at the end of every business day, redemption at par within two business days, segregated reserves of short Treasuries, repos or deposits, and monthly CPA examinations.

legislation.title: Digital Financial Assets Law
legislation.citation: California Financial Code Division 1.25 (as amended by AB 1934)
legislation.summary: From 2026-07-01, digital financial asset business activity with California residents needs a DFPI licence (or an application filed by that date).

legislation.title: New York Banking Law, Article 13-B (transmitters of money)
legislation.summary: No one may engage in the business of selling or issuing payment instruments, or of receiving money for transmission or transmitting money, in New York without a licence from the Superintendent of Financial Services (§ 641). Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: California Money Transmission Act
legislation.citation: California Financial Code Division 1.2 (§ 2000 and following)
legislation.summary: No one may engage in the business of money transmission in California without a licence from the DFPI (§ 2030), unless exempt. Section numbers and exemptions to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Alabama Monetary Transmission Act
legislation.citation: Ala. Code Title 8, Chapter 7A (§ 8-7A-1 and following)
legislation.summary: No one may engage in money transmission in Alabama, or advertise or hold out as providing it, unless licensed by the Alabama Securities Commission or an authorized delegate of a licensee (§ 8-7A-5). Replaced the Sale of Checks Act. Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Alaska Uniform Money Services Act
legislation.summary: Money transmission in Alaska needs a licence from the Division of Banking and Securities (AS 06.55.101), with a surety bond (AS 06.55.104) and net worth. Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Arizona Money Transmission Modernization Act
legislation.citation: A.R.S. Title 6, Chapter 12 (§ 6-1201 and following), as replaced by S.B. 1580 (2022)

legislation.title: Arkansas Uniform Money Services Act
legislation.summary: Money transmission in Arkansas, defined to include virtual currency, needs a licence from the Securities Department (§ 23-55-201) unless excluded (§ 23-55-103); surety bond (§ 23-55-204) and tangible net worth (§ 23-55-207), as amended by Act 442 of 2023.

legislation.title: Colorado Money Transmission Modernization Act
legislation.citation: C.R.S. Title 11, Article 110 (§ 11-110-101 and following), enacted by H.B. 25-1201
legislation.summary: Repealed and re-enacted Colorado's money transmitter law as the Money Transmission Modernization Act (approved April 18, 2025). Money transmission in Colorado needs a State Banking Board licence (§ 11-110-501) unless exempt (§ 11-110-301); tangible net worth (§ 11-110-1001) and surety bond (§ 11-110-1002). Effective date to verify; the article is repealed September 1, 2030 unless continued (§ 11-110-1203).

legislation.title: Connecticut money transmission law
legislation.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 36a-595 to 36a-614 (as amended by Public Acts 24-146 and 25-66)
legislation.summary: Money transmission in Connecticut, including covered virtual currency activity, needs a licence from the Banking Commissioner unless exempt (§ 36a-609). Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Delaware Money Transmission and Virtual Currency Modernization Act
legislation.citation: 5 Del. C. Chapter 23 (§ 2301 and following), 85 Del. Laws c. 338
legislation.summary: Replaced Delaware's earlier sale of checks and money transmission chapter. Money transmission (§ 2304) and virtual-currency business activity (§ 2335) need a licence from the State Bank Commissioner unless exempt (§ 2305). Effective or application date to verify (85 Del. Laws c. 338, § 3).

legislation.title: District of Columbia Money Transmission Code
legislation.summary: No one may engage in the business of money transmission in the District of Columbia without a DISB licence (§ 26-1002) unless exempt (§ 26-1003); net worth (§ 26-1004) and bond or other security device (§ 26-1007).

legislation.title: Florida money services businesses law
legislation.citation: Fla. Stat. Chapter 560 (Part II, money transmitters)
legislation.summary: Acting as a money transmitter, including for virtual currency (§ 560.103), in, from or into Florida needs an OFR money services business licence under Part II; net worth and surety bond (§ 560.209). Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Georgia Sellers of Payment Instruments and Money Transmitters
legislation.citation: O.C.G.A. Title 7, Chapter 1, Article 4 (§ 7-1-680 and following)
legislation.summary: Money transmission in Georgia, with virtual currency defined in § 7-1-680, needs a licence from the Department of Banking and Finance unless exempt (§ 7-1-682); tangible net worth and bond (§ 7-1-683.2). legislation.title: Idaho Money Transmitters Act

legislation.title: Illinois Uniform Money Transmission Modernization Act
legislation.summary: No one may engage in the business of money transmission in Illinois without a licence from IDFPR unless exempt. legislation.title: Illinois Digital Assets and Consumer Protection Act
legislation.summary: Digital asset business activity with or on behalf of an Illinois resident needs IDFPR registration unless exempt; businesses have until 2027-07-01 to register (transition section 35-15). Signed 2025-08-18. Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Indiana Money Transmission Modernization Act
legislation.summary: Indiana's adoption of the CSBS model Money Transmission Modernization Act, without its virtual currency portion, replacing IC 28-8-4 from 2024-01-01. legislation.title: Iowa Uniform Money Transmission Modernization Act
legislation.summary: No one may engage in the business of money transmission in Iowa without a licence (533C.301) unless exempt (533C.103); NMLS is used for licensing (533C.302); kiosk and digital financial asset exchange rules in 533C.1004. legislation.title: Kansas Money Transmission Act
legislation.citation: Kansas Money Transmission Act, enacted by 2024 HB 2560 (replacing the Kansas Money Transmitter Act, K.S.A. 9-508 et seq.); codified sections to verify
legislation.summary: Repeals and replaces the Kansas Money Transmitter Act; money transmission in Kansas needs a licence from the State Bank Commissioner unless exempt. Approved by the Governor on 2024-04-19; effective date and section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Kentucky money transmitters law
legislation.summary: No one may engage in money transmission in Kentucky without a licence or acting as a licensee's authorized delegate (KRS 286.11-005). Short title (commonly cited as the Kentucky Money Transmitters Act of 2006) and section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Louisiana Money Transmission Act

legislation.summary: Replaces the Sale of Checks and Money Transmission Act from 2026-07-01, based mainly on the CSBS model Money Transmission Modernization Act; money transmission in Louisiana needs an OFI licence unless exempt. Codified section numbers to verify against legis.la.gov.

legislation.title: Louisiana Virtual Currency Businesses Act
legislation.summary: Requires an OFI licence to engage in virtual currency business activity in Louisiana; passed in 2020, with unlicensed activity prohibited after 2023-07-01. Licence section number to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Maine Money Transmission Modernization Act

legislation.summary: Short title § 6067; licence required § 6087; exemptions § 6074; net worth § 6100-R; surety bond § 6100-S; virtual currency business activity licence § 6100-QQ (subchapter 13). Replaced the repealed money transmitter subchapter of chapter 80. Effective date to verify.

legislation.title: Maryland Money Transmission Act

legislation.summary: Money transmission in Maryland needs a licence from the Commissioner of Financial Regulation; amended by 2021 SB 219 (effective 2021-10-01). OFR treats virtual currency as monetary value under the Act. Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Massachusetts money transmission law

legislation.title: Michigan Money Transmission Services Act
legislation.summary: No one may provide money transmission services in Michigan without a licence (MCL 487.1011); net worth and surety bond in MCL 487.1013. Amended effective 2019-03-28. Current text to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Minnesota Money Transmission Modernization Act
legislation.summary: Recodified chapter 53B as the Money Transmission Modernization Act (signed 2023-05-24); money transmission, including virtual currency business activity, needs a Commerce licence unless exempt. Kiosk requirements added by Laws 2024, ch. 114, art. 3 (effective 2024-08-01). Section numbers and effective date to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Mississippi Money Transmission Modernization Act
legislation.summary: Money transmission in Mississippi needs a DBCF licence (licensing requirements § 75-16-25; control persons and key individuals § 75-16-27). Amended in 2026 by HB 1596 and HB 1625 (virtual currency kiosks, effective 2026-07-01). Effective date of the Act to verify.

legislation.title: Missouri Money Transmission Modernization Act of 2024

Text to verify against the statute.

legislation.title: Nebraska Money Transmitters Act

legislation.title: Nevada Revised Statutes, Chapter 671 (money transmission)

legislation.title: New Hampshire RSA Chapter 399-G, Licensing of Money Transmitters

legislation.title: New Jersey Money Transmitters Act
legislation.summary: Licensing of money transmitters and foreign money transmitters by the Department of Banking and Insurance (P.L. 1998, c. 14). Net worth and bond as stated in DOBI's application form; section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: New Mexico Uniform Money Services Act
legislation.summary: Licensing of money transmitters (§ 58-32-201), check cashers (§ 58-32-301) and currency exchangers (§ 58-32-401); money transmission defined in § 58-32-102; money transmitter surety bond in § 58-32-203. Section numbers from the Division's pages; to verify against the statute.

legislation.title: North Carolina Money Transmitters Act

legislation.title: North Dakota Century Code chapter 13-09.1, Money Transmitters

legislation.title: Ohio Revised Code Chapter 1315, transmitters of money

legislation.title: Oklahoma Money Transmission Modernization Act

legislation.summary: Digital asset kiosk operators must hold an Oklahoma money transmitter licence, with kiosk-specific duties (location notices, quarterly kiosk reports, transaction limits). Amended by HB 3521 to refer to the new Act.

legislation.title: Oregon Money Transmitters Act

legislation.title: Pennsylvania Money Transmission and Virtual Currency Transmission Business Licensing Law (Money Transmitter Act, Act 249 of 1965)
legislation.citation: Act of 1965, No. 249, as amended by Act 7 of 2025 (codified at 7 P.S. § 6101 and following; to verify)
legislation.summary: No one may engage in the business of transmitting money, or (from 2025-08-26) virtual currency by means of a transmittal instrument for a fee with or on behalf of an individual, without a licence from the Department of Banking and Securities (Section 2). legislation.title: Rhode Island currency transmission (licensing of currency transmitters)
legislation.summary: Currency transmission, including maintaining control of virtual currency on behalf of others (§ 19-14-1), needs a licence from the Department of Business Regulation; chapter 19-14.3 adds permissible investments, virtual currency disclosures, property interests and kiosk rules. legislation.title: South Carolina Uniform Money Services Act
legislation.citation: S.C. Code Ann. § 35-11-100 and following (as amended by 2024 Act No. 218)
legislation.summary: Money transmission in South Carolina needs a licence from the Attorney General as Commissioner (§ 35-11-200); 2024 Act No. 218 substantially adopted the Money Transmission Modernization Act, applying to existing licensees from 2025-01-01.

legislation.title: South Dakota money transmission
legislation.summary: Money transmission in South Dakota needs a Division of Banking licence; tangible net worth (§ 51A-17-99), surety bond (§ 51A-17-100) and like-kind virtual currency holdings (§ 51A-17-109). Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Tennessee Money Transmission Modernization Act

legislation.summary: Replaced Title 45, Chapter 7 from 2024-01-01; no one may engage in money transmission in Tennessee without a licence (§ 45-7-110(a)).

legislation.title: Texas Money Services Modernization Act
legislation.summary: Money transmission in Texas needs a Department of Banking licence (§ 152.101); stablecoin pegged to and redeemable for sovereign currency is money or monetary value (§ 152.003(19)).

legislation.title: Utah Money Transmitter Act
legislation.summary: No one may engage in the business of money transmission in Utah without a licence unless exempt (§ 7-25-202); money transmission does not include a blockchain token (§ 7-25-102). Section numbers to verify against the source.

legislation.title: Vermont Money Services
legislation.citation: 8 V.S.A. chapter 79 (as rewritten by Act 110 of 2024 and amended by Act 142 of 2026)
legislation.summary: No one may engage in money transmission, which includes virtual-currency business activity, without a licence (§ 2505); subchapter 10 sets virtual currency duties; virtual currency kiosks prohibited from 2026-07-01 (§ 2577).

legislation.title: Virginia Money Transmitters (Chapter 19.1)
legislation.citation: Va. Code § 6.2-1922 and following (2025 Acts ch. 214, HB 1942)

legislation.title: Washington Uniform Money Services Act

legislation.summary: Virtual currency transmission for Washington residents is money transmission needing a licence; virtual currency is not a permissible investment, and licensees must hold like-kind virtual currency owed to consumers.

legislation.title: Wyoming special purpose depository institutions

license_types.name: Money services business registration (money transmitter)
license_types.scope: A registration with FinCEN, not a licence: it covers no state by itself. Money transmission (of US dollars or convertible virtual currency) needs a licence in each state, and each state's money transmitter licence counts only alongside this registration (FIN-2019-G001 for convertible virtual currency).
license_types.coverage_note: Covers nowhere by itself (covers: []): in law this is a federal registration, not a licence, and doesn't replace state money transmitter licences. State money transmitter licence types require it (requires). Production's model may hold the same registration as fincen_money_services_business or fincen_msb_registration; the state licences accept any of the three ids. Assumption to verify: that every licensed money transmitter Mynt relies on must register (some exemptions, e.g. for banks, are not modelled).
